# Guideline server

> A server that keeps a team's shared coding-agent guidelines (per-stack rules, skills, subagents, MCP settings). In a project, the `guideline` CLI picks and receives guidelines as copies in `.guideline/`, and `guideline apply` composes the ruler sources (`.ruler/`) from them; edits go back as proposals. This server's address is {{SERVER}}.

This document is the guide agents and people read when they first use this server.

## Setup (once per machine)

1. You need Node 24 or later and the `guideline` CLI (the `guideline-manage` npm package, 0.24 or later):

   ```bash
   npm install -g guideline-manage
   ```

   To use it straight from a clone of its repository, call `node <repo>/cli/bin/guideline.js <command>`.

2. Log in. If the server is public (`PUBLIC_READ=1`, the default), fetching guidelines (pick/update/list) works without a login, so you only need one to send proposals. When the browser opens, log in with the admin token and click "Issue". A read token is stored in `~/.config/guideline/credentials.json` (mode 600).

   ```bash
   guideline login --server {{SERVER}}
   ```

   - Without a browser, store a token issued on the web "Tokens" page with `guideline login --server {{SERVER}} --token-stdin`.
   - **Uploading proposals needs a token with the `propose` scope.** An admin issues it on the web "Tokens" page; store it with `--token-stdin`.
   - With an `admin` scope token, `guideline propose` applies directly instead of proposing. `login` shows the stored token's scope when it saves it, and `guideline status` shows it on its "Token:" line (`token` with `--json`).
   - Where files cannot be written, as in CI, use the `GUIDELINE_TOKEN` environment variable.
   - The server address is chosen in this order: `--server` > the project's `guideline.json` > the `GUIDELINE_SERVER` environment variable.
   - The language of CLI messages and of the text written into projects is `GUIDELINE_LANG`, then `lang` in `~/.config/guideline/config.json` (default `en`).

## Receiving guidelines in a project

**Only projects that use ruler can receive guidelines** — the unit directory must have `.ruler/` (otherwise commands stop with "Not a ruler project"). Run commands in that directory.

```bash
guideline pick                 # open the server form; submitting applies the choice right away
guideline pick --recommend r.json   # open the form with blocks an agent chose ({"block key": "reason"}) already checked
guideline pick --new <name>    # new project: create GUIDELINE_PROJECTS_DIR/<name>, git init, then apply (a path works too)
guideline status               # are the applied guidelines current, and what did the project change?
guideline update               # same items, latest version. Files edited in the project are skipped
guideline update --force       # also overwrite files edited in the project
guideline apply                # compose the generated agent files from .guideline/ without the server, then run ruler
guideline pick --local         # change only what you receive (personal scope, needs git); committed files stay as they are
```

- `pick` sends only the result of comparing the project with the source to the server and prints the form address (`Form: <address>` on stderr). It waits until items are checked in the form and submitted. MCP values (secrets) are not sent.
- The form chooses **whole stacks**, not single files. A stack with child stacks (`browser/browseros-neo` inside `browser`) shows them as a tree, each with its `when` (the work that needs it). Checking a child stack checks its ancestors too, marked "Ancestor" (the ancestor's own files come with it); checking a parent does not check its children; unchecking an ancestor unchecks its descendants. Unchecking a child also unchecks the ancestors that were checked only because of it, unless you checked them yourself, another chosen child stack is still under them, or another chosen block needs them (`requires`).
- Form states: "same" is already applied, "different" means the project copy differs from the source (turn on "update" to overwrite it), "missing" is not there yet (check it to add). Unchecking an existing item means "remove". The form goes step by step — guidelines, MCP, subagents, skills, review — and category buttons only filter the items shown (checks do not change). Blocks a chosen block requires (`requires`) are checked too.
- A domain stack `<tool>__<domain>` (e.g. `deploy-package__gitlab.develma.com`) holds the rules for using that tool on that server. Pick only stacks whose domain matches the server the project uses.
- **Where things go.** Received copies are written as they are in the source, in `.guideline/`: guidelines in `.guideline/rules/<stack>/NN-*.md` (`.guideline/rules/<parent>/<child>/` for a child stack), skills in `.guideline/skills/<name>/`, subagents in `.guideline/agents/`, MCP servers in `.guideline/mcp/<name>/`, and each source's management additions in `.guideline/management/<source>.md`. Overrides are in `.guideline/overrides/<stack path>/`. The project's ruler settings are in `.ruler/ruler.project.toml`.
- **Generated files.** `guideline apply` composes what ruler reads from `.guideline/`: `.ruler/<stack>/NN-*.md` and the index `.ruler/<stack>/99-reference.md`, `.ruler/guideline.md` (the management guideline), `.ruler/skills/`, `.ruler/agents/`, `.ruler/ruler.toml` (`ruler.project.toml` plus the received MCP servers) and `docs/guideline/` (reference guidelines and setup docs). They are listed in a block in `.gitignore` (`# START guideline generated files` … `# END guideline generated files`) and are not committed. After composing, `apply` runs `ruler apply` at the git root (when ruler is installed). `pick` and `update` do the same at the end.
- **Commit** `guideline.json` (chosen items), `guideline-lock.json` (applied revision and hashes), `.guideline/`, `.ruler/ruler.project.toml`, `.gitignore` and the project's own `.ruler/*.md`. The CLI does not commit.
- **After a clone or in a new worktree**, the generated files do not exist yet. Run `guideline apply`: it needs no server. A project with a `package.json` that has `guideline-manage` in its dependencies runs it from `scripts.prepare`, so `pnpm install` does it. Do not run `ruler apply` alone before that: without `.ruler/ruler.toml` ruler writes files for every agent, including a `CLAUDE.md` that hides `AGENTS.md` from Claude Code (`apply` deletes such a file and says so).
- **Moving an old project.** The first `pick` or `update` with this CLI moves a project that was received in the old layout (copies in `.ruler/<stack>/` and `docs/guideline/`): copies go to `.guideline/` with the project's edits kept, overrides to `.guideline/overrides/`, `ruler.toml` to `ruler.project.toml`, old copies are removed from the git index (`git rm --cached`), and `prepare` in `package.json` changes from `ruler apply` to `guideline apply` only when `guideline-manage` is in its dependencies and `ruler apply` has no arguments. Otherwise you get a `dev-dependency` (or `prepare-manual`) to-do, which `status` and `update` repeat until it is fixed: until then, `prepare` in a clone runs only ruler and writes an `AGENTS.md` without the guidelines. It stops with "Commit or stash your changes first" when tracked files in the directory have uncommitted changes. Review with `git status` and commit. Until the move, `status`, `propose` and `apply` stop with exit code 2 ("This project still uses the old layout"), and an old CLI cannot read the new files.
- **Monorepos**: run in a subdirectory with its own `.ruler/` and that directory becomes a separate unit, with its own manifest, lock and copies. Skills, subagents and MCP servers are received only at the git root. ruler builds that directory's guidelines only when the git root's ruler settings (`.ruler/ruler.project.toml`) have `nested = true`. `guideline apply` at the git root also composes every unit below it that git tracks (a directory with a committed `guideline-lock.json`), then runs ruler once, so one `apply` (or the root's `prepare`) after a clone fills every unit. `update`, `pick` and `pick --local` at the git root compose those units too, before ruler runs. A unit still in the old layout is skipped (to-do `unit-update`), and a unit whose generated files could not all be written gets `unit-write-failed`. When the git root is not a guideline project itself, `apply` there composes the units and runs ruler with the root's own `.ruler/ruler.toml` (to-do `root-ruler-toml` when there is none). A unit's own `apply` stops before ruler (to-do `root-apply`) while the git root has no `.ruler/ruler.toml`.
- Exit codes: 0 done, 1 error, 2 usage error (including "not a ruler project", and `apply` in a project that has not received anything yet or is still in the old layout), 3 cancelled or expired (nothing written). A source whose server is too old for the stack form (older than 0.24.0) is skipped with "This server is older than the CLI" and counts as an error (exit code 1).

## Receiving from several sources

One project can receive from several guideline servers (sources). For example, tool stacks from a personal server and company stacks from a company server.

```bash
guideline pick --source personal --server https://my.example.dev     # add a source and pick in its server's form
guideline pick --source company --server {{SERVER}}
guideline pick                       # opens each source's form in turn (a cancelled source stays as it was)
guideline update --source company    # update only that source
```

```json
{
  "version": 3, "form": "ruler", "agents": ["claude", "codex"],
  "sources": {
    "personal": { "server": "https://my.example.dev", "items": ["rules/base"] },
    "company": { "server": "{{SERVER}}", "items": ["rules/base", "rules/browser", "rules/browser/browseros-neo"], "aliases": { "rules/base": "company-base" } }
  }
}
```

- `items` are block keys (`rules/<stack path>`, `skills/<name>`, `agents/<name>.md`, `mcp/<name>`), and a child stack comes with its ancestor stacks. Do not write file paths.
- When two sources give the same name (stack, skill, subagent, MCP server), `pick` stops with "Name clash" (exit code 2, nothing written). Give one source an alias in `aliases`, `"<unit>": "<new name>"` (the unit is `rules/<top-level stack>` — child stacks follow their top-level stack's alias — `skills/<name>`, `agents/<name>.md` or `mcp/<name>`), and it is received under that name: `.guideline/rules/company-base/` (composed into `.ruler/company-base/`), the skill's `name:` line, `[mcp_servers.<new name>]` in `ruler.toml`.
- Store a token per server with `guideline login --server <URL>`. With several sources, `GUIDELINE_TOKEN` is not used.
- If one source's server cannot be reached, that source is left as it is, the rest is applied, and the exit code is 1.
- `propose` sends one proposal per source to that source's server (aliases are turned back into the original names).
- Each source's `docs/management.md` is kept in `.guideline/management/<source>.md` and appended to the management guideline (`.ruler/guideline.md`) as `## <source> additional guidelines`.

## Only on your machine (personal scope)

A worker can add blocks to the project's choice, or remove blocks from it, for themselves only. The project and its committed files stay as they are.

```bash
guideline pick --local                       # the personal form: As project / Add / Remove per block
guideline pick --local --recommend r.json    # pre-checked: {"add": {"block key": "reason"}, "remove": {"block key": "reason"}}
```

- **Where it is kept.** The personal selection is `local.json` in git's common directory, `<git common dir>/guideline/units/<unit key>/` (unit key `%root` for the git root unit, otherwise the URL-encoded unit path, such as `packages%2Fapi`). Every worktree of the clone shares it, and it is never committed. The personal copies (`.guideline/` and `guideline-lock.json`) live next to it. It needs a git repository and git 2.31 or later; otherwise `pick --local` stops with exit code 2.
- **What you receive** = the project's choice + your additions (with their ancestor stacks) − your removals (with the child stacks below them). `guideline.json`, `guideline-lock.json`, `.guideline/` and the `.gitignore` block do not change. Generated files that come only from the personal scope are listed in git's `info/exclude`, in a block per unit and worktree (`# START guideline personal files <unit path> @<worktree>`, `.` for the git root unit and for the main worktree).
- **Required.** In the project's pick form a chosen block can be marked **Required** (`sources.<name>.required` in `guideline.json`). Nobody can remove a Required block, or a stack that holds one, in a personal selection; a removal left from before is ignored (to-do `personal-ignored`).
- **Recommending for a worker.** Judge from the worker's own work and tools, not from the project's files: a stack whose `when` names a tool ("work that uses <tool>") fits a worker who uses that tool. A plain `{"block key": "reason"}` means add. A key not in the source, or a removal of a Required block, stops with exit code 2 before the form opens.
- **Machine defaults.** "Save this selection as my default" in the personal form stores it per server address (origin) in `~/.config/guideline/defaults.json` (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/guideline/` when it is set). It only pre-checks the personal form in a project where you have no personal selection yet; `update` and `apply` never read it.
- **Updating.** `pick --local` receives the personal copies at the revision in the project's lock. `guideline update` updates the project and the personal copies together. `guideline apply` composes them in any worktree without the server. Do not edit the personal copies: `update` overwrites them and `propose` does not send them.
- **Setup.** A stack received only personally gets a `setup-personal` to-do instead of `setup`: set it up without changing committed files, and tell the user about a step that would.
- `guideline status` shows the personal scope on two lines ("Personal scope — added …", "removed …"); `status --json` has `personal` (`null` when the unit is not in a git repository or `local.json` cannot be read).
- A server older than 0.24 does not know the personal form: `pick --local` stops with exit code 1 ("This server does not know the personal form").

## Sending changes upstream (proposals)

The source changes through proposals an admin accepts. With an `admin` scope token, `propose` applies directly instead of proposing (the source changes right away, without review); add `--review` to get a review. Once the source changes, each project receives it with `guideline update`.

```bash
guideline propose --dry-run              # show edited copies turned back into source form (not sent)
guideline propose --title "<title>"      # send them as a proposal (applied directly with an admin token; --review proposes)
guideline source <empty folder>          # get a working copy of the source to write new guidelines in
guideline propose --from <that folder> --title "<title>"   # send what was added, changed or deleted there
guideline proposals                      # list your proposals (--status pending|accepted|rejected)
guideline proposals <number>             # one proposal: Outdated and conflicts, each file's diff (--json: the server's response)
```

- `propose` sends only copies in `.guideline/` that are "edited in project" according to the lock. Copies are already in source form, so they are sent as they are; skills and MCP servers send each file's change, addition or deletion. Edit an MCP server in `.guideline/mcp/<name>/server.json`. A received MCP table that was edited in `.ruler/ruler.project.toml` is not sent, and `status` shows it as current.
- Write new guidelines, skills or MCP servers into a folder from `guideline source`, at their source paths (`rules/<stack>/NN-*.md`, `skills/<name>/`, `mcp/<name>/server.json` and so on), then send them with `propose --from`. The writing rules are that folder's `docs/authoring.md`. Agents use the `guideline-export` skill.
- Admins review the diff under "Proposals" on the web and accept, reject or edit it. If the source changed in the meantime, non-overlapping changes are merged; overlapping ones make the proposal Outdated and it cannot be accepted.
- `guideline proposals` shows your own proposals; with an `admin` scope token it shows every proposal, so an agent can review them. Accepting and rejecting are on the web or through the API.

## What agents do

`pick --json`, `update --json`, `status --json` and `apply --json` print `{ revision, written, deleted, todos }` (`status` only carries the to-dos it can tell). Whatever the CLI could not do alone is left in `todos`. Handle them one by one and report what you handled and what is left. **Submitting the form is the user's confirmation, so do not ask again before applying.**

A to-do with `scope: "personal"` comes from the personal copies (`setup-personal`, `removed-upstream`, and others whose message starts with "Personal copy —"). Handle it like the same kind, but do not change committed files for it; tell the user about a step that would.

| kind | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `mcp-build` | Following the "Build on apply" section of `data.text` (the source `mcp/<name>/README.md`), read this project's values and build the MCP entry in `.ruler/ruler.project.toml` (`.ruler/ruler.toml` is regenerated by `guideline apply`). Show the values and where they came from and get confirmation before writing |
| `env` | Tell the user which environment variables to set (`data.vars`) and how to obtain them per the README |
| `setup` | Check `## Check` in `docs/guideline/<stack>/SETUP.md`; if it is not done, go through `## Setup` with the user |
| `conflict` | The same name already exists and differs from the source. Show the diff and let the user choose (turn on update in the next `pick`) |
| `skipped` | Skipped because the project edited the file. Ask whether to send it upstream with `guideline propose` or overwrite it with `update --force` |
| `override` | An override section points at a file or section the source does not have. Fix the override section's first line |
| `override-unchosen` | `.guideline/overrides/<stack>/` belongs to a stack that is not chosen, so it was not composed. Ask whether to pick the stack or delete the override |
| `subagents-off` | The subagent has a copy in `.guideline/` but was not composed. Ask whether to turn on `[agents] enabled = true` in `.ruler/ruler.project.toml` (it adds generated files to `.gitignore`), then run `guideline apply` |
| `apply` | The generated agent files are out of date (from `status`, or after a move that could not write them). Run `guideline apply`; it needs no server. Run it before committing, or `git add -A` puts the old copies back |
| `ruler-apply` | Ask whether you may run the suggested `ruler apply` command |
| `root-apply` | A monorepo unit's `apply` did not run ruler because the git root has no `.ruler/ruler.toml` yet. Run `guideline apply` at the git root first (or put `.ruler/ruler.toml` with `nested = true` there yourself), then run it in the unit again |
| `unit-update` | `guideline apply`, `update`, `pick` or `pick --local` at the git root found a unit below it still in the old layout and did not compose it. Run `guideline update` in that unit (it needs the server) |
| `unit-problem` | `guideline apply`, `update`, `pick` or `pick --local` at the git root could not open a unit below it (the reason follows). Fix it, or run `guideline apply` in that unit to see the error |
| `unit-write-failed` | `guideline apply`, `update`, `pick` or `pick --local` at the git root could not write all the generated files of a unit below it (the error names the unit). ruler still ran, so do not trust that unit's `AGENTS.md` and other agent files. Fix the cause, then run `guideline apply` at the git root again |
| `root-ruler-toml` | The git root is not a guideline project and has no `.ruler/ruler.toml`, so `apply` composed the units but did not run ruler. Ask the user to put a `.ruler/ruler.toml` with `nested = true` there and commit it, then run `guideline apply` again |
| `nested-off` | Ask whether to turn on `nested = true` in `.ruler/ruler.project.toml` at the git root |
| `no-copy` | A chosen item has no copy in `.guideline/` (blocked, or an MCP entry to build), so it was not composed. Run `guideline update` to see why |
| `mcp-conflict` | A received MCP table was not added to `.ruler/ruler.toml`: the project's `ruler.project.toml` already has a table with that name (the project's own is kept), or the TOML shape clashes. Show the table and let the user resolve it. If the project changed a received MCP table, edit `.guideline/mcp/<name>/server.json` and send it with `guideline propose`; the changed table stays in `ruler.project.toml`; `status` shows the MCP as current but repeats this to-do |
| `untracked` | A file is now generated but git still tracks it, or the CLI removed it from the git index (`git rm --cached`, the file stays on disk), or it could not ask git and gives a command. Show the command and, with the user's go-ahead, run it; tell the user to check `git status` and commit |
| `stray-ruler-output` | ruler ran without `.ruler/ruler.toml` (usually `ruler apply` right after a clone) and wrote a file for every agent. The CLI deleted `CLAUDE.md` because it carries ruler's marker, or kept it because it has none or because the settings do not tell (a `default_agents` list over several lines). Tell the user; if it was kept, check whether it hides `AGENTS.md` from Claude Code and ask before deleting it. Only `CLAUDE.md` is checked: other agents' files ruler wrote may remain |
| `migrated` | The project moved to the new layout. Tell the user what moved, and that they should review with `git status` and commit. Handle the other to-dos |
| `manifest-v3` | `guideline.json` was rewritten as version 3 (whole stacks), so the rest of each chosen stack's files were added. Tell the user, and commit `guideline.json` with the rest |
| `prepare` | `prepare` in `package.json` now runs `guideline apply` instead of `ruler apply`. Show the change; the user reviews and commits it |
| `dev-dependency` | `guideline-manage` is not in this project's dependencies, so `prepare` was left alone: until it is, `prepare` in a clone runs only ruler and writes an `AGENTS.md` without the guidelines. Run the command shown (add it as a dev dependency), then `guideline apply`, which changes `prepare`. `status` and `update` repeat it until it is fixed |
| `prepare-manual` | `prepare` in `package.json` runs `ruler apply` with arguments, which `guideline apply` does not take, so it was left alone. Show it; the user changes it to `guideline apply` by hand (ruler settings go in `.ruler/ruler.project.toml`). `status` and `update` repeat it until it is fixed |
| `apply-hook` | There is no `package.json`, so nothing composes agent files after a clone. Add `guideline apply` to the project's setup step (for Orca, `scripts.setup` in `orca.yaml`) |
| `adopted` | A copy `propose` left out. It already differed from the source when first received (it may be an old version). Use `guideline propose --only <item>` only if the project really edited it; if it is an old version, `guideline update --force` |
| `alias` | An alias problem. For "the stack moved", move the override files to `.guideline/overrides/<new name>/`. Otherwise fix `aliases` in `guideline.json` |
| `removed-upstream` | Tell the user, and suggest `guideline pick` to remove it (`guideline pick --local` when it has `scope: "personal"`) |
| `setup-personal` | A stack received only in the personal scope has a setup doc. Follow `docs/guideline/<stack>/SETUP.md` as for `setup`, but do not change committed files (`package.json`, committed config, `.gitignore`, `.ruler/ruler.project.toml` …). Do not skip a step that would silently: tell the user what it would change |
| `personal-ignored` | The project now marks a block Required that the worker removed personally, so the removal is ignored. Tell the user; clean it up with `guideline pick --local` |
| `personal-shadowed` | A personal addition has the same final name as a block the project picked from another source, so it is not received. From `pick --local` it was not saved; otherwise clean it up with `guideline pick --local` |
| `personal-revision` | The personal copies and the project's copies are at different revisions of a source (another worktree ran `update`), so overrides may point at sections that differ. Run `guideline update` |
| `personal-sync` | The personal copies could not be updated (a write error, or a personal lock that cannot be read: delete the file named). The project was applied. Fix it and run `guideline update` again |
| `local-bad` | The personal selection (`local.json`) cannot be read, so the files were composed from the project's choice only. The user fixes or deletes that file, then run `guideline apply` |
| `override-target` | An override points at a file or section that is not in the composed copies (the project's plus the personal ones). Fix the override's first line, or run `guideline update` when the revisions differ. Any project can get it |
| `missing-requires` | A received block (`item`) needs blocks that were not received (`data.missing`; from `update` and `status`). Tell the user which blocks are missing, and run `guideline pick --recommend <file> --json` with a recommendation file holding them (add `--source <source>` when there are several sources); submitting the form is the confirmation |
| `blocked` | Not applied because of a source warning (or because it is a nested directory), or a file in `.guideline/` could not be composed (the message gives its path). The copy stays as it is. Report the reason |
| `leftover` | Unchecked, or dropped from a chosen stack by the source, but the copy differs from the source, so it was not deleted. Show the diff and ask whether to delete it |

## Rules

- **Do not edit the copies in `.guideline/` directly** (everything there except `overrides/`), nor `guideline.json` and `guideline-lock.json`: the CLI writes them. To share an edit, send it with `guideline propose`.
- **Do not edit the generated files** (`.ruler/<stack>/`, `.ruler/guideline.md`, `.ruler/skills/`, `.ruler/ruler.toml`, `docs/guideline/`): the next `guideline apply` overwrites them. Settings of ruler go in `.ruler/ruler.project.toml`.
- **Do not put project files inside `.guideline/rules/<stack>/` or the generated `.ruler/<stack>/` folders** (sub-folders included). A received stack folder belongs to the source: a file or sub-folder that is not in the source shows up as "removed from source". Project-only rules are overrides, below, or `.ruler/*.md`.
- Write anything that should differ for this project only as an **override**: `.guideline/overrides/<stack path>/override.md` (or `override.d/*.md`; `.guideline/overrides/<parent>/<child>/override.md` for a child stack). Start each override with the line ``Overrides: `<stack>/<file>` "<## section title>"`` (drop the quoted title for the whole file). Overrides win over the copies, and the CLI never touches them.
- When a stack needs setup, follow `docs/guideline/<stack>/SETUP.md`. For a stack in the personal scope (`setup-personal`), do not change committed files.
- **Do not edit the personal copies** in `<git common dir>/guideline/units/`: `guideline update` overwrites them and `propose` does not send them. Change what a worker receives with `guideline pick --local`.
- Never put secrets in proposals either. Write MCP values as `${VAR}` references.

## API (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`)

- [Health]({{SERVER}}/api/v1/health): no authentication. Server version, schema, API level, latest revision
- `GET {{SERVER}}/api/v1/whoami`: the sent token's `{ kind, name, scope }` (the admin token is `{ kind: "admin", name: null, scope: "admin" }`). No token or a wrong one is 401, even on a public server
- `GET {{SERVER}}/api/v1/catalog`: stacks, skills, subagents, MCP servers, their categories (`categories`) and display names (`labels`, same keys as categories)
- `GET {{SERVER}}/api/v1/archive?rev=<revision>`: the whole source (tar.gz)
- `GET {{SERVER}}/api/v1/files/<path>?rev=<revision>`: one source file
- `POST {{SERVER}}/api/v1/proposals`: a proposal (`propose` scope token). Body `{ title, description?, project?, changes: [{ path, text | base64 | delete: true, base: <sha256> | null }] }`. An admin token or an `admin` scope token can use `apply: true` to apply it right away without review. From the CLI, `guideline propose` applies directly by default with an admin token (`--review` proposes)
- `GET {{SERVER}}/api/v1/proposals?status=<pending|accepted|rejected>`: the list of your proposals (an `admin` scope token sees all)
- `GET {{SERVER}}/api/v1/proposals/<number>`: one proposal with `outdated`, `conflicts` and `changes: [{ path, kind, base }]`; your own, or any with an `admin` scope token (otherwise 404). `?diff=1` adds each change's `diff` (unified diff from the base to the proposal, `null` when not text); `?content=1` adds the content as `text`, `base64` or `delete: true`, as in the upload body. They can be combined
- `POST {{SERVER}}/api/v1/proposals/<number>/accept`, `POST {{SERVER}}/api/v1/proposals/<number>/reject` (body `{ note? }`): accept or reject a proposal (admin token or `admin` scope token). A conflict is 409 with `conflicts`

## More

- [Web]({{SERVER}}/): anyone can view guidelines and their history (log in if the server is private); editing, reverting, reviewing proposals and issuing tokens need a login with the admin token
- `docs/manual/en/getting-started.md` in the repository: the user guide for people (all documents: `docs/manual/README.md`)
